name: Diclofenac
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Diclofenac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) cleared by liver metabolism; its pharmacokinetics do not change in kidney impairment. The kidney concern is injury, not accumulation: the US label advises avoiding it in advanced kidney disease unless benefits outweigh the risk and monitoring kidney function, potassium and blood pressure in anyone at risk.
kidney_function_basis: Label PK study used inulin clearance (60–90, 30–60, <30 mL/min); warnings use 'advanced renal disease' without a number. Mapping 'advanced' to CrCl <30 is our judgment.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose by indication: osteoarthritis 100 to 150 mg/day, rheumatoid arthritis 150 to 200 mg/day, in divided doses (label). Lowest effective dose, shortest duration.

No dose change (pharmacokinetics unchanged; label). Kidney impairment raises the risk of NSAID kidney injury: monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure; avoid volume depletion and the ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic combination.
bands.short: No dose change; monitor SCr, K, BP

bands.recommendation: No information from controlled studies in advanced kidney disease; avoid unless benefits outweigh the risk of worsening kidney function, and if used monitor kidney function (label, Renal Toxicity). Pharmacokinetics are unchanged in kidney impairment (inulin clearance down to <30 mL/min), so the risk is kidney injury, not accumulation.

hd.text: Avoid unless benefits outweigh the risk (advanced kidney disease; label). Not removed by dialysis (over 99% protein-bound). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Avoid unless benefits outweigh the risk (label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury.

dialyzable: Unlikely: hemodialysis may not be useful because of high protein binding (over 99%; label).
monitoring: Creatinine, potassium and blood pressure in CKD, heart failure, liver disease, dehydration or with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics. Liver enzymes within 4 to 8 weeks of starting long-term use (diclofenac hepatotoxicity warning).

renal.recommendation: Not approved for children; kidney dosing not applicable.

adult: PH: 50 mg enteric-coated tablets (main), 25 and 100 mg SR, 25 mg/mL injection (IM/IV), gel, suppositories. The kidney advice applies to systemic forms; topical gel has low systemic exposure (not addressed by this label).
Diclofenac potassium and sodium forms are not bioequivalent mg for mg (label).
Label: transaminases within 4 to 8 weeks of starting.
